title: Check yourself: pattern matching for instanceof

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A method reads `if (!(o instanceof Invoice inv) || inv.lines().isEmpty()) { audit(o); } else { send(inv); } return inv.number();`. Its class has no field or other variable named inv. What does javac 21 say about the two later uses of inv?

options.text: It accepts both, since inv stays in scope from where the pattern declares it to the end of the method
options.says: a pattern variable is scoped by where the test is known to be true, not by the block around it

options.text: It accepts both, since the else branch and the line after the if run only once o is an Invoice
options.says: the line after the if is also reached after the if body ran, when the test failed

options.text: It accepts send(inv) and rejects the return, since the line after the if is also reached when the test failed
options.says: the else of a negated test has inv in scope; after an if whose body falls through, inv is not in scope

options.text: It rejects send(inv) and accepts the return, since a variable from a negated test is in scope only after the if
options.says: the else of a negated test is exactly where the test was true, so inv is in scope there

origin.section: A Pattern Variable Exists Only Where the Match Is Certain

questions.stem: Inside a method: `if (o instanceof String path) { path = path.strip(); uploads.submit(() -> store(path)); }`. What happens when the class is compiled with javac 21?

options.text: It fails at path = path.strip(), since a pattern variable is final whether or not it is declared final
options.says: a pattern variable is not implicitly final; only `instanceof final String path` forbids the assignment

options.text: It fails at the lambda, since path is assigned after the pattern binds it and is not effectively final
options.says: a reassigned pattern variable is an ordinary local that is no longer effectively final, so a lambda can't capture it

options.text: It compiles, and the task stores the stripped value, since the lambda captures path after its last assignment
options.says: a lambda can capture only a final or effectively final local, and a reassigned one is neither

options.text: It compiles, and the task stores the unstripped value, since the lambda captures the object that o was tested with
options.says: the lambda would capture the variable path, not o; and here it doesn't compile at all

origin.section: A Pattern Variable Exists Only Where the Match Is Certain

questions.stem: Class Uploader has `private final String bucket = "archive";` and the method `String bucketFor(Object hint) { if (!(hint instanceof String bucket) || bucket.isBlank()) { log("bad hint"); } return bucket; }`. What does bucketFor("invoices-2026") do?

options.text: It returns "invoices-2026" without logging, since the hint matched, and the line after the if reads what the pattern bound
options.says: after an if whose body can complete, the pattern variable is not in scope, so the name means the field

options.text: It returns "archive" without logging, since the hint matched, and the line after the if reads what the field holds
options.says: the test was false, so nothing is logged, and the return reads the field because the pattern variable is out of scope there

options.text: It never runs, since javac rejects a pattern variable that has the name of a field of the class
options.says: a pattern variable is a local, and a local may shadow a field; only another local of the same name is an error

options.text: It never runs, since javac rejects a name used after an if whose body can complete
options.says: that is an error only when no other variable has the name; here the field does, so it compiles

origin.section: Out of Its Scope, a Pattern Variable's Name Means the Field

questions.stem: A service built with --release 21 has a field `Map<String, Locale> prefs` and the method `Locale pick(String user) { if (prefs.get(user) instanceof Locale chosen) return chosen; return Locale.ROOT; }`. What happens for a user with no entry in prefs?

options.text: pick returns Locale.ROOT, since the test is false for a null value even though its type always fits
options.says: instanceof is false for null whatever the pattern, so the absent entry falls through to the default

options.text: pick returns null, since a pattern whose type always fits matches every value of that type, null included
options.says: an unconditional pattern is unconditional about the type only; instanceof is still false for null

options.text: The build fails, since javac rejects a pattern whose type the declared type already guarantees
options.says: Java 16 to 20 rejected it; Java 21 accepts it

options.text: The call fails, since binding chosen casts the null value before the test can look at it
options.says: the pattern tests before it binds, and it is a null check: an absent entry falls through to the default

origin.section: Since Java 21 a Pattern of the Declared Type Compiles, and It Is Still False for null

concepts: A pattern variable is an ordinary local: reassignable unless declared final, and once reassigned a lambda can't capture it; a local of the same name is a compile error.

A pattern variable is in scope only where the test is known to be true: after &&, in the true branch of ?:, in the else of a negated test, and after a statement that can't finish while the test is false; not after || or &, and not after a negated if that falls through.
Since Java 21 a pattern whose type the declared type already guarantees compiles, and instanceof is still false for null, so it acts as a null check that binds.
